prompt.name: Name the channel
prompt.base_url: Optional. Enter a relay API URL, e.g. one relayed through Cloudflare. The {model} variable is supported, e.g. https://api.example.com/v1/{model}/chat
prompt.key: Enter the authentication key for this channel
prompt.proxy: Proxy for this channel only; http and socks5 are supported, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:1080. Put `%s` in the proxy URL as a session placeholder: it is replaced with a unique session ID derived from the key.
prompt.test_model: Model used to test the channel; tests are unavailable when empty. Chat models only, e.g. gpt-3.5-turbo
prompt.models: Select the models this channel supports. You can also use a * wildcard, e.g. gpt-3.5* matches every model starting with gpt-3.5. The * may only appear at the end and must follow at least one character: gpt-3.5* is valid, *gpt-3.5 is not.
prompt.model_mapping: Model mapping: each line forwards the model name the user requests to the real upstream model name (e.g. opus-latest → claude-opus-4.8). Billing uses the real upstream model by default; tick "Bill on incoming" to bill by the requested name instead (price it under model pricing first).
prompt.model_headers: Custom request headers per model, e.g. {"key": "value"}
prompt.header_override: Pass client request headers through to the upstream. A value can be a fixed value, {api_key} (the channel key) or {client_header:X-Request-Id} (the client header of that name). Use * as the key to pass through every client header, or start the key with re: or regex: to pass through headers matching a regular expression. Note: authentication headers are handled by the channel and are never overridden. Use standard header casing for keys (e.g. X-Request-Id) so the same header is not sent with different casing.
prompt.custom_parameter: Inject extra parameters as JSON (nesting allowed). Control options: overwrite: true replaces fields of the same name; when unset or false, only missing fields are added. per_model: true applies the overrides per model name, e.g. {"per_model":true,"gpt-3.5-turbo":{"temperature": 0.7},"gpt-4":{"temperature": 0.5}}. pre_add: true applies the overrides as soon as the request arrives instead of just before it is sent upstream; works for all channels (including Claude and Gemini), e.g. {"pre_add":true,"overwrite":true,"stream":false}.
prompt.groups: Select the user groups this channel serves
prompt.only_chat: With chat only selected, requests that include function calls skip this channel
prompt.provider_models_list: Fill in all fields before fetching the model list
prompt.tag: Tag the channel to manage channels in bulk by tag. Note: once a tag is set, some settings can only be changed through the channel tag, not from the channel list.
prompt.pre_cost: Choose the pre-billing option used to estimate cost. If counting images takes too many resources, you can turn off image billing. Note: some channels return no token counts when streaming, which makes input token counts inaccurate.
prompt.disabled_stream: Models listed here have streaming disabled: streaming requests for these models skip this channel
prompt.allow_extra_body: When on, extra fields in the user's request (such as the OpenAI SDK's extra_body parameter) are passed through, for sending custom parameters to the upstream API
prompt.pass_through_body: When on, the client request body is forwarded upstream as is: only the mapped model name is rewritten, and unknown fields and the original bytes are kept. Useful for transparent proxying over the same protocol. Note: only OpenAI-protocol channels honor this (channels that build their own body, such as Claude and Gemini, ignore it); when on, extra-field merging is skipped (only the channel extra parameters still apply, at byte level).
prompt.allow_service_tier: When off (default), request fields that make the upstream charge more are dropped before forwarding: OpenAI service_tier priority, fast and ultrafast, and Claude speed fast and inference_geo us. Turn on only if users should be able to request these tiers. Either way, requests are billed at the tier the upstream reports (fast and priority 2x, ultrafast 6x, flex 0.5x, US-only inference 1.1x).
prompt.unified_request_response_model: When on, the model name in responses is the one the user requested instead of the mapped model name. Note: the global switch in system settings takes precedence; when it is on, it overrides this channel setting.
prompt.balance_threshold: When the upstream balance refreshed by the balance check falls below this amount, a notification is sent once through the configured notify channels; it is sent again only after the balance recovers above the threshold and drops again. 0 disables the alert. Only channel types with a balance API are refreshed (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, DeepSeek, Moonshot, SiliconFlow). OpenRouter reports the remaining amount of this key, so set a spend limit on the key in the OpenRouter dashboard.
prompt.apiVersionExample: Enter the default API version, e.g. {{example}}
prompt.keyFormatBaidu: Use the format APIKey|SecretKey. If the OpenAI API plugin is enabled, enter the API key directly
prompt.manageKeyOpenAI: Optional. An OpenAI admin key reads the organization's daily cost report, to compare with what this site expected. Official API only.
prompt.manageKeyAnthropic: Optional. An Anthropic Admin API key (sk-ant-admin...) reads the organization's daily cost report, to compare with what this site expected. Official API only.
prompt.manageKeyOpenRouter: Optional. An OpenRouter management key shows the balance of the whole account and reads its daily cost report; without it only the limit of the key above is shown.
prompt.manageKeyRequesty: Optional. A Requesty key with manage permission shows the organization balance; the key above is tried when this is empty.
prompt.manageKeyVolcengine: Optional. The account's AccessKey as AccessKeyID|SecretAccessKey shows the balance; the Ark API key cannot read it.
prompt.keyFormatAws: Use the format Region|AccessKeyID|SecretAccessKey|SessionToken (SessionToken is optional). AssumeRole mode: Region|AccessKeyID|SecretAccessKey|RoleArn (put arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/ROLE_NAME in the fourth field; temporary credentials are fetched and renewed automatically). Role chaining: Region|AccessKeyID|SecretAccessKey|SessionToken|RoleArn. Or Region|BearerToken
prompt.dashscopePlugin: Enter the plugin parameters, i.e. the value of the X-DashScope-Plugin request header
prompt.speechRegion: Enter the location/region of your Speech Studio, e.g. eastasia
prompt.proxyKey: Enter the {{service}} key; if it has no key set, any value works
prompt.proxyAddress: Enter the address where {{service}} is deployed
prompt.cozeModels: Model names take the form coze-{bot_id}; you can also use the coze-* wildcard to match every model starting with coze
prompt.cozeMapping: Model name mapping: use an easy-to-remember name instead of coze-{bot_id}, e.g. {"coze-translate": "coze-xxxxx"}. Note: with model mapping, the model names above must be the pre-mapping names; in this example, add coze-translate to the models (not needed if you already use coze-*).
prompt.ollamaUrl: Enter the address of your Ollama deployment, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434. If you use Cloudflare Zero Trust, enter the access credentials in the plugin settings below

prompt.siliconflowUrl: The official API URL https://api.siliconflow.com is being retired; use https://api.siliconflow.cn
prompt.oauthJson: Enter the full OAuth2 credential JSON, or click "OAuth authorization" below to fetch it automatically
prompt.claudeOauth: Enter an access_token (sk-ant-sid01-xxx) or the full OAuth2 credential JSON, or click "OAuth authorization" below to fetch it automatically
prompt.gcpProjectId: Enter the Google Cloud project ID, e.g. my-project-123
prompt.projectIdOptional: Optional. Leave blank to detect it automatically or generate one at random, e.g. my-project-123
prompt.vertexExpressKey: Enter an API key (from the Google Cloud Console)
prompt.remark: A note for admins, such as where the key comes from or when it expires. Kept per channel and not shared across a tag.
prompt.need2response_models: One model per line (commas also work). Chat completions requests for these models are sent to the Responses API and converted back. Entries are added to the built-in list (o1-pro, o3-pro, o3 / o4-mini deep research, codex-mini-latest); put - before a model to stop converting it on this channel, for upstreams that serve it on chat completions. Leave empty to use the built-in list.

form.name: Model name
form.nameHint: What clients put in the model field, e.g. auto/coder.
form.nameHelp: Letters, digits and . _ / - only, up to 100 characters, not starting or ending with /. It must not collide with an existing model. The name shows up in /v1/models and can be used in token and organization allow lists like any model.
form.displayNameHint: Shown in the catalog instead of the model name.
form.decisionModelHint: Classifies the first user message. A decision model is recommended: it answers with a probability for every label. A small, fast chat model also works. Charged to the caller once per session.
form.question: Question
form.questionHint: Give the decision model a sentence of context, then ask the question the labels answer.
form.questionHelp: Keep it short: the labels and their descriptions carry most of the meaning. Do not put long instructions here; the output format is fixed by the gateway.
form.routesHint: Each label is one answer to the question, mapped to the model that should handle it.
form.routesHelp: 2 to 16 routes. Labels must be distinct; overlapping labels split the probability and push requests to the fallback. Describe the request, not the model. Targets must be models, not other policies.
form.routeDescriptionPlaceholder: What kind of request this label covers
form.fallbackModelHint: Used when confidence is below the threshold, the decision fails, or the first message has no text. Put your safest model here.
form.thresholdHint: 0 to 1. Below it the request goes to the fallback.
form.thresholdHelp: 0.5 is a good start. Raise it to send more borderline requests to the fallback; lower it to trust the decision model more. With logprobs scoring the confidence is the label's probability; self-reported confidence is only a ranking.
form.pinTtlHint: How long a session keeps the model chosen at its first message. 0 classifies every request.
form.pinTtlHelp: Later turns of a pinned session skip the decision, keep the upstream prompt cache warm and never switch models mid-conversation. Sessions are identified by the session header, Claude Code metadata, prompt_cache_key or the prompt prefix.
form.maxInputCharsHint: The first message is cut to this length before classification. 0 uses the default (4000).
form.decisionTimeoutHint: On timeout the request goes to the fallback. 0 uses the default (3000).

missing.name: Model name is required
missing.routes: At least two routes, each with a label and a target model

form.scoringHint: How the decision model's confidence is measured.
form.scoringHelp: Logprobs reads the model's real probability for each label, so the threshold is a probability. It needs a non-reasoning model on a channel that returns logprobs (OpenAI-compatible APIs such as GPT-4.1, DeepSeek in non-thinking mode, or self-hosted vLLM); Claude, reasoning models and most aggregator gateways do not return them.
